                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of a thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain, acyclovir and famciclovir are ineffective as they require thymidine kinase for activation. Ganciclovir, although activated by a different kinase, is not the most effective choice due to its toxicity profile and less favorable pharmacokinetics for this indication. Cidofovir does not require viral kinase for activation, making it effective against thymidine kinase-deficient strains and a better choice for treating this population. Amantadine is irrelevant as it targets influenza viruses, not varicella-zoster. Therefore, cidofovir is the best antiviral agent to treat the elderly population infected with this strain at the retirement home.
